content:
Customs officers persuaded a man to come down safely after he climbed atop the metal structure in the pedestrian lane of International Bridge I and threatened to jump toward the Rio Bravo, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, which based its account on eyewitness testimony at the scene.

The incident unfolded near the middle of the viaduct on the Puente de las Américas, which connects Laredo, Texas, with Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, and drew alarm from pedestrians crossing north to south, the outlet reported. El Mañana placed the episode within the perimeter under United States jurisdiction.

One officer with the Oficina de Aduanas y Protección Fronteriza (U.S. Customs and Border Protection) approached cautiously and spoke with the man for several minutes until he agreed to descend, according to the report. Additional Customs officers then secured him on the ground and secured the perimeter.

Officers asked the man whether he was from Mexico or the United States; El Mañana did not report his answer. He was taken under strict custody toward U.S. territory, and pedestrian traffic on the bridge resumed minutes later, the outlet reported.

The man was not named in the report, and no age or nationality was given. Anyone in crisis in the United States can call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, “Momentos de angustia en el Puente I; agentes evitan que un hombre salte al río Bravo en el paso peatonal,” October 28, 2026
